bib.title: Process for Adapting Language Models to Society (PALMS) with Values-Targeted Datasets
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2021 (35th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems)

question: Can a small, hand-curated dataset that reflects a predetermined set of values be used to fine-tune a pretrained language model so that its behaviour on sensitive topics measurably shifts toward those values?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning a pretrained LM on a small values-targeted dataset will move outputs toward the target values, more so for larger models, without hurting capabilities.
contributions: PALMS: an iterative 7-step process (topic selection, desired behaviour description, prompt creation, completion creation, fine-tuning, evaluation, iterate) for building a values-targeted dataset
Evaluation with toxicity scoring, human ratings of value adherence, and co-occurrence analysis, against base and control models across GPT-3 sizes
Evidence that effectiveness grows with model size and capability integrity is largely preserved

method.summary: Authors wrote 80 Q&A prompts and had a professional writer produce 40-340 word completions matching written position statements on eight sensitive-topic categories. GPT-3 models of eight sizes were fine-tuned on these via the OpenAI fine-tuning API, then compared with base models and models fine-tuned on a 100-snippet control corpus using Perspective API toxicity, 1-5 human ratings and co-occurrence word analysis.
method.task: supervised fine-tuning of a pretrained LM for behaviour/value alignment

limits: Only U.S. English, U.S.-law and UN-rights positions; authors say behaviour is a template, not universal
Test prompts only Q&A and leading open-ended prompts; small window into model behaviour

Statistical test for significance asterisks not described; one round of iteration; single run, no seeds stated
Capability integrity only on 175B and a subset of GPT-3 evals; GLUE/SuperGLUE skipped
Whether the effect equals few-shot context stuffing is left open
